# Optia Data

> Optia Data is a data and AI consultancy that harmonises syndicated market, retailer and internal data into governed commercial reporting for consumer goods, retail, financial services, education, engineering and healthcare organisations.

Optia Data Ltd, registered in England and Wales, company number 15884308, incorporated 7 August 2024. Locations in London, Barcelona, Nuremberg, Abu Dhabi, Bangalore, Chicago, New York. Data processes certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022. Every delivered output has a named analyst behind it.

## About

- [Company information](https://optiadata.com/company-data/): full company record, services, expertise, industries, markets, data sources and case study index.
- [Companies House record](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/15884308): registered company details.

## Services

- **Foundation: the right data**: Optia Data brings syndicated market data, retailer data and internal systems into one harmonised, analysis-ready baseline. Discrepancies are caught and resolved before they reach category reporting, a board pack or a buyer meeting.
- **Context: giving the data meaning**: Optia Data applies each client's own category definitions, hierarchies and commercial measures to the harmonised baseline, so market, brand, retailer and internal figures can be compared without averaging across incompatible periods or definitions.
- **Intelligence: knowing what to do next**: Optia Data builds reporting, dashboards and analysis on the governed baseline, and recommends where predictive modelling, workflow automation or AI assistance genuinely fits rather than applying it by default.
- **Governance and data engineering**: Optia Data runs client data processes in a code-versioned and data-versioned setup with full lineage of every change. Every delivered output has a named analyst behind it who has checked the number.

## Case studies

Fifteen published engagements. Fourteen name the client; one financial services engagement is published without a client name.

- [Arla Foods](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/arla-foods/): Arla Foods replaced a 20-day monthly reporting process with an always-ready view of market, brand, category and retailer performance across 16 markets, cutting production of monthly market reporting from 20 days to around 10 minutes.
- [Campari UK](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/campari/): Campari UK brought on-trade and off-trade performance into one Total Trade view across four reconciled data sources and 14 dashboard pages, while preserving the differences between the two channels. Campari's own team now runs the monthly refresh.
- [Starbucks EMEA](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/starbucks-emea/): Starbucks EMEA consolidated 33 monthly reports into one automated model covering 16 markets, reconstructed 13 missing periods to restore trend history, and designed three intelligence perspectives around different commercial questions.
- [Bacardi](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/bacardi/): Bacardi connected eight source systems into automated management reporting and combined two trade channels into one total trade view, removing more than 40 hours a month of manual reporting and taking key processes from days to minutes.
- [Australian Vintage](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/australian-vintage/): Australian Vintage identified and corrected GBP 26 million of misclassified category sales, recovered around 793 SKUs missing from a data delivery, and reduced monthly validation and publication from days to hours across 11 pages of analysis.
- [Golden Acre Foods](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/golden-acre-foods/): Golden Acre Foods brought four major retailers into one consistent weekly view, rebuilt 104 weeks of category and retailer history, completed and matched around 2,700 records, and cut time spent preparing commercial reports by 30 per cent.
- [Samworth Brothers](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/samworth-brothers/): Samworth Brothers replaced a fragmented monthly reporting process with one commercial model spanning six categories, 16 benchmarked competitors and five external data sources harmonised with internal reporting, reclaiming around a week from every monthly cycle.
- [Vit Hit](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/vit-hit/): Vit Hit turned complex market data into a self-serve commercial view covering three categories, three market levels from total grocery to impulse and discounters, five performance measures and three years of weekly history.
- [International Beverage](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/international-beverage/): International Beverage is turning a manually assembled monthly leadership pack into an automated process spanning six data sources, 20 markets and 156 weeks of history, with the UK, the US and China as priority countries.
- [Samyang Foods](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/samyang-foods/): Samyang is replacing fragmented monthly reporting with one commercial model connecting sell-out, sell-through and sell-in across five European markets, targeting the removal of two days per market of manual Excel preparation, with first dashboards six weeks from sign-off.
- [QTS Data Centres](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/qts-data-centres/): QTS replaced an expert-built spreadsheet process with a constraint-based maintenance plan for a 45MW hyperscale data centre, coordinating three build phases and 12 equipment classes, then compressed twelve months of work into nine and a half when the build programme changed.
- [Inspired Learning Group](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/inspired-learning-group/): Inspired Learning Group turned fragmented finance, occupancy, admissions and payroll data from five source systems into role-specific reporting across around 25 schools and nurseries, at five reporting levels from individual setting to group.
- [Henkel](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/henkel/): Eleven adhesives and stationery categories were brought into one commercial view covering six brands down to individual SKU, three major UK grocers and two years of weekly history. Delivered by the team now operating as Optia.
- [A Tier-One Global Bank](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/tier-one-global-bank/): Optia Data supports the client data management and risk assessment processes behind a major bank's KYC operation, covering 30,000 records processed, 20 countries within the wider programme scope, a daily activity feed for continuous access auditability, and zero Priority 1 incidents during peak processing windows. The client is not named.
- [Oracare Group](https://optiadata.com/case-studies/oracare-group/): Oracare Group created a consistent monthly view across a multi-country practice estate, bringing three practice brands into one reporting model delivered from a consolidated source, without changing how individual practices operated.
